content:
# Report: region_011 (3,000 bp, region.fasta)

**Sequence:** 3,000 bp DNA; A/C/G/T only; overall GC 47.9%. Flanking GC skews are near zero, so this is not obviously part of a GC-AT boundary or horizontial-island edge.

## Notable features

**1. A single strong protein-coding ORF, c.1161–2177 (plus strand).** One ORF dominates all six frames: 1,017 nt starting with ATG at 1161 and ending with TGA at 2177, encoding a 338-aa protein of plausible composition (Leu/Ala/Gly-rich, no stop-internal oddities). Supporting evidence it is a genuine gene rather than chance:
- Its GC content is ~55–57% (e.g. 56.7% over 1350–1500) versus ~42–47% in the flanking upstream segment — a hallmark of coding DNA.
- A candidate ribosome-binding site **AAGGA at c.1127–1131**, ending 30 nt (≈10 bp) upstream of the ATG — well within the 5–13 bp spacing typical of bacterial Shine–Dalgarno sites.
- The protein shows no signal peptide or transmembrane helix (no 19-residue window with mean hydropathy > 1.6), so it is predicted to be cytosolic.
- The 15–20 nt after the stop codon (c.2178–2195) is AT-rich and terminates the ORF cleanly; the most plausible −35/−10 promoter elements upstream (c.1000–1160) are imperfect, consistent with the promoter lying outside the fragment.

Coordinates: **ORF 1161–2177 (+ strand); RBS 1127–1131**.

**2. Possible origin-of-replication-like GC-skew shift, c.1500–1900.** In 700-bp sliding windows, GC skew goes from consistently negative (≈ −0.03 to −0.10) upstream of ~1500 to positive (up to +0.04) over ~1600–1900, then decays. Note this coincides with the coding region, so some of the shift is likely just codon usage of the gene; still, the sign change at ~c.1500–1600 is worth flagging if this fragment lies near a replication origin.

**3. The reverse strand.** No reverse-strand ORF exceeds 240 aa (longest: 2048–2764 minus-strand, 239 codons; and 307–786, 160 codons). Given the plus-strand ORF covers both of those intervals, these are almost certainly ignorable nested frames.

**4. Repeats/motifs.** No repeats above the 6–8-mer background level, no long palindromes (≥14 bp), no obvious stem-loop terminator-like structures — nothing striking.

## Bottom line
The region is essentially **a compact single-gene locus**: one ~1 kb bacterial-style protein-coding ORF at **c.1161–2177** with a putative SD site at **c.1127–1131**, predicted to encode a 338-aa cytosolic protein, embedded in otherwise featureless AT-rich flanking sequence (~c.1–1160 and 2178–3000). Without database access I can't assign a function, but the protein's high Gly/Lys content around its mid-section and lack of membrane signals are consistent with a soluble metabolic/regulatory enzyme. If you can share taxonomic context (species, GC% of genome), that would sharpen the promoter and codon-usage interpretation.
